conclusion: Selected gameplay, bone/paint/RNG workload, endpoint pixels, draw counts, PWA/audio and GPU query completeness pass. Overall performance and total-resource nondegradation are not established: four-pair intervals include zero, and B ordinal4 has a renderer-resource mismatch of unknown cause despite identical recorded scene/private-owner snapshots. No sample or mismatching trial is discarded.

resourceValidation.scope: Read-only observations outside timed frames; these equalities are recorded, not included in the original workload acceptance guard

resourceFinding.hypothesis: Different renderer registration/retention history is compatible with identical recorded object graphs, but no allocation/disposal identity ledger was recorded. No captured owner field identifies the four geometries or one texture. Similar counters also differed within the historical baseline; neither a source-only cause nor a warmup-only cause is established.
resourceFinding.limits: Renderer geometry/texture/program counters span renderer registrations and cache/target allocations, not only G.scene. Equal scene or private graph counts/dimensions do not establish equal uploaded object identities, retirement histories or VRAM bytes.

submit.method: Four adjacent paired-trial relative effects; two-sided Student t interval, df=3. Assumes independent, approximately normal pair effects. Shared browser/process, chronological and host-throttling effects remain possible; not hardware inference or a predefined noninferiority test.

limitations: Chromium SwiftShader is software-rendered; no physical-PC, mobile, Nintendo Switch, thermal or power measurement.
Exact supplied Git SHAs are verified against every production build input and served artifact; no production bytes are rewritten.
Both variants must naturally install and activate their service worker and report a complete offline snapshot before setup/warmup; this is steady-state enabled PWA, not a cold-start timing test.

Completed-frame throughput includes synchronous 1-pixel readback, serializes CPU/GPU work, excludes display scanout and deferred DOM/audio completion, and is not ordinary game FPS or input-to-photon latency.
One unchanged PlayerController and seven unchanged BotBrains execute.
The inherited eight-live-actor stress fixture replaces controller/brain output intents with stationary outward fire. This is not ordinary human movement input coverage.
The native scheduler is frozen; one complete fixed-60Hz simulation frame runs per diagnostic rAF. Dynamic resolution is held at 1.
Eight ABBA/BAAB trials must pass the original strict workload, endpoint pixel, controller, PWA and audio guards. Mismatch is unresolved; no acceptance guard is relaxed.
Endpoint full image parity is checked, not every measured image. Console page errors fail the trial.
Passed means only the explicitly selected gameplay/pixel/PWA/audio guards. Draw/resource/private-owner equality and performance nondegradation are separately recorded and require review.

Heap/CDP and renderer resource snapshots bracket the transaction without forced GC; the ending CDP snapshot also includes endpoint capture/serialization. Their deltas are observations, not pure-loop allocation, a lifetime leak or GPU-memory proof.

Optional disjoint WebGL2 elapsed queries add identical observation work to both variants. Only valid recovered queries are summarized; incomplete subsets are not whole-run GPU percentiles. SwiftShader timer durations are not hardware GPU evidence.
Resource mismatch ordinal4(B) remains unresolved and is retained with all raw samples.
Pooled percentiles/means are descriptive. Four paired-trial effect intervals include zero; no predefined overall noninferiority test or resource acceptance threshold was passed.
Candidate worst completed frame is 1843ms versus baseline1706.1ms, despite lower pooled p99.
Chronological/shared browser and observed cgroup CPU-throttle effects remain possible confounders, not a proved explanation of any timing/resource difference.

Native source-display uses separate MeshStandardMaterial; the custom level material in this whole-game scenario is the native ink overlay. Authored custom grate-backface validation remains a separate fixture.
